question: What are the trunks made of?
html:
Fair Harbor trunks are made from recycled plastic bottles, at about 11 bottles per trunk (Fair Harbor public filings). By the end of 2021, the brand had recycled a cumulative 26M bottles (Fair Harbor public filings).

What the material is

  • Source material: post-consumer plastic bottles, recycled into the fabric (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Bottles per trunk: about 11 (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Cumulative bottles: 26M through 2021 (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Brand position: the recycled-material story anchors the move from a swim brand to a year-round sustainable lifestyle brand (Fair Harbor growth plan).

What we can't confirm yet

The context has no full fabric spec. These details are missing:

QuestionData that would answer it
Exact fabric blend (e.g., % recycled content, stretch fibre)Current product tech packs and fabric supplier spec sheets
Liner materialProduct spec sheets by style
Whether every trunk style uses the same fabricStyle-level bill of materials across the live catalogue
Whether non-swim lines (golf, kids, collegiate) use recycled inputsBills of materials for the 2025 and 2026 launches
Bottle count after 2021An updated recycling tally from the company or its mill

The 26M figure dates from 2021. A current count would need a fresh company source. The research behind this answer is dated Sept 24, 2026 and Oct 6, 2026.

How this fits the range

  • 64.0% of the 372 live products are now non-swim (Fair Harbor growth plan). So the bottle story covers a shrinking share of the catalogue unless the newer lines use similar inputs.
  • Swim is the most-returned category at Shopify brands, at 21.6% (Fair Harbor growth plan). Fit and fabric feel are likely drivers (est.). The context does not break out return reasons for Fair Harbor.

The recycled-bottle story is what lets Fair Harbor sell at full price into golf pro shops, campus bookstores and coastal specialty doors. That matters because 38.5% of live variants are marked down today and the growth plan depends on growing from ~250 doors to ~520 (Fair Harbor growth plan).

Next actions

  1. Pull current tech packs and supplier spec sheets for every live trunk style. Publish one verified material line per product.
  2. Get an updated cumulative bottle count from the company or its fabric mill to replace the 2021 figure.
  3. Audit the golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom bills of materials. Confirm which non-swim products carry recycled content.
  4. Tag swim returns by reason code (fit, fabric feel, other). This would test whether material drives the 21.6% category return benchmark at Fair Harbor.
